idea: Executive coaching for senior women in finance
buyer: Senior women in asset management and banking, or their employers
pain: Progression stalls at senior levels and internal support is thin
channel: Her network and husband's banking contacts
verdict: Employer funding lifts the price meaningfully, but coaching is unprotectable and she is not a trained coach.

why.distribution: Warm across both networks, and employers are receptive to the theme.
why.demand: Firms do fund coaching for senior women; the budget genuinely exists.
why.fmf: She has the lived experience but no coaching qualification, which employers often require.
why.defensibility: Executive coaching is a crowded, credentialled market.
why.tailwind: Diversity and retention budgets are real and defended.

ceiling_arithmetic: £6k x 33 programmes = £198k, roughly 200 sessions - beyond part-time capacity. Realistic: 10-14 = £60-84k.
carries: Employer-funded pricing well above self-funded coaching, with a defended budget line.
kills: No coaching credential in a credentialled market, and one-to-one delivery caps the year.
test: Ask three HR or D&I leads what they pay for external coaching and what they require.
test_pass: They would engage her without accreditation.
